name: Rolex
tagline: The crown of Swiss watchmaking and the world's most recognised luxury watch
summary: Rolex is the largest and most valuable luxury watch brand in the world, known for robust, vertically integrated Oyster watches such as the Submariner, Daytona and Datejust. Owned by a charitable foundation, it combines conservative evolutionary design with in-house everything, from gold alloys to hairsprings.
history:
Rolex began in London in 1905, when Bavarian-born Hans Wilsdorf and his brother-in-law Alfred Davis founded Wilsdorf & Davis to import Swiss movements and case them as wristwatches, then still seen as a fad. Wilsdorf registered the Rolex name in 1908, and in 1910 a Rolex became the first wristwatch to receive an official Swiss chronometer certificate. High wartime taxes pushed the company to Geneva in 1919.

The 1920s and 1930s defined the brand. The hermetically sealed Oyster case of 1926 was publicised when Mercedes Gleitze wore one while swimming the English Channel in 1927, and the Perpetual self-winding rotor followed in 1931. After the war came the Datejust (1945), the Submariner and Explorer (1953), the GMT-Master (1955), the Day-Date (1956) and the Cosmograph Daytona (1963), a family of professional and classic models that still forms the core catalogue.

When Wilsdorf's wife died in 1944 he created the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, and on his death in 1960 it became the sole owner of Rolex, which remains private and does not publish figures. Rolex weathered the quartz crisis by staying with mechanical watches, briefly offering the quartz Oysterquartz, and by positioning itself as a status symbol rather than a mere instrument.

Since the 2000s Rolex has integrated its supply chain almost completely, casting its own gold and platinum alloys, making Parachrom hairsprings and Cerachrom ceramic bezels, and introducing a new generation of calibres with the Chronergy escapement. Its 2023 purchase of the retailer Bucherer and the Rolex Certified Pre-Owned programme show a move into distribution. Industry estimates put annual output above one million watches and sales above CHF 10 billion, several times its nearest rival, and demand for its steel sports models has outstripped supply for years.

name: Tudor
tagline: Rolex's sister brand, reborn as the go-to modern tool watch
summary: Founded by Hans Wilsdorf to offer Rolex-grade reliability at a lower price, Tudor has become one of the fastest-growing Swiss brands on the strength of the vintage-inspired Black Bay and titanium Pelagos. It now makes its own movements through its sister company Kenissi.
history:
Tudor traces its origins to 1926, when the Geneva firm Veuve de Philippe Hüther registered the name 'The Tudor' on behalf of Hans Wilsdorf, the founder of Rolex. Wilsdorf took over the brand in 1936 and in 1946 created Montres Tudor SA, explaining that he wanted a watch retailers could sell at a more modest price while keeping the dependability of Rolex. Early Tudors used bought-in movements but Rolex Oyster cases, crowns and bracelets.

The Oyster Prince of 1952 was tested by the British North Greenland Expedition, and the Tudor Submariner of 1954 went on to serve with navies including the French Marine Nationale and the US Navy. In the 1970s Tudor introduced the snowflake hands on its divers and launched the Oysterdate chronographs later nicknamed 'Monte Carlo'. As the brand drifted, it withdrew from the United States in the mid-1990s.

A reinvention began in the late 2000s. The Heritage Chrono of 2010 and especially the Black Bay of 2012, which revived vintage Submariner cues such as the big crown and snowflake hands, turned Tudor into a collector favourite. The Pelagos titanium diver followed the same year and Tudor returned to the US market in 2013. In 2015 it introduced its first manufacture calibre, the MT5621, and in 2016 set up Kenissi to produce movements for itself and other brands such as Breitling, Chanel and Norqain.

The Black Bay Fifty-Eight of 2018, sized at 39mm, became a modern classic, and in 2023 the Black Bay received METAS Master Chronometer certification. Tudor now sits alongside Rolex under the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, with independent design and its own headquarters in Geneva, offering Swiss-made tool watches mainly between roughly $3,000 and $7,000.

name: Omega
tagline: The Moonwatch maker and official timekeeper of the Olympic Games
summary: Omega is the Swatch Group's flagship luxury brand, famous for the Speedmaster that went to the Moon, the Seamaster worn by James Bond and its long role as Olympic timekeeper. It pioneered the co-axial escapement and METAS Master Chronometer certification.
history:
Omega began in 1848 when 23-year-old Louis Brandt set up a watch assembly workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds, buying parts from local craftsmen and selling finished watches across Europe. His sons Louis-Paul and César moved the business to Biel/Bienne in 1880 and adopted industrial, in-house production. Their 19-ligne 'Omega' calibre of 1894, with interchangeable parts, was so successful that the company took the name Louis Brandt & Frère – Omega Watch Co. in 1903.

Omega merged with Tissot in 1930 to form SSIH and in 1932 became official timekeeper of the Los Angeles Olympics, a role it has held at most Games since. Post-war icons followed: the Seamaster (1948), Constellation (1952) and the Speedmaster (1957). NASA qualified the Speedmaster for manned missions in 1965, and on 21 July 1969 Buzz Aldrin wore one on the lunar surface. The following year a Speedmaster helped time the critical engine burn that brought Apollo 13 home.

The quartz crisis hit SSIH hard. In 1983 it merged with ASUAG to create SMH, reorganised by Nicolas Hayek and renamed the Swatch Group in 1998. Under the group Omega was repositioned upmarket, supported by product placement in the James Bond films from GoldenEye (1995) onwards.

In 1999 Omega industrialised George Daniels' co-axial escapement, and in 2015 it launched Master Chronometer certification with the Swiss federal metrology institute METAS, testing complete watches to 15,000 gauss of magnetism. Today, headquartered in Biel, Omega is widely estimated to be the second-largest Swiss luxury watch brand by sales after Rolex.

name: TAG Heuer
tagline: Avant-garde Swiss chronographs with deep roots in motor racing
summary: TAG Heuer is LVMH's high-volume sports-luxury brand, built on Heuer's pioneering stopwatches and chronographs. The Carrera and square Monaco are motor-racing icons, backed by long partnerships in Formula 1 and motorsport.
history:
Edouard Heuer opened a watchmaking workshop in Saint-Imier in 1860 and moved to Biel in 1867. In 1887 he patented the oscillating pinion, a clutch system still used in many mechanical chronographs. The company built its reputation on precision timing: the 1916 Mikrograph measured 1/100th of a second, and Heuer stopwatches timed the 1920, 1924 and 1928 Olympic Games.

Under Jack Heuer, great-grandson of the founder, the brand became synonymous with motor racing. The Carrera, named after the Carrera Panamericana road race, arrived in 1963, followed by the Autavia and, in 1969, the square, waterproof Monaco, one of the first automatic chronographs thanks to the Calibre 11 developed with Breitling, Hamilton-Büren and Dubois Dépraz. Steve McQueen wore a Monaco in the 1971 film Le Mans, and Heuer timed Ferrari's F1 team in the 1970s.

The quartz crisis left Heuer struggling, and in 1985 it was acquired by Techniques d'Avant Garde (TAG), a Luxembourg-based holding of the Ojjeh family, becoming TAG Heuer. The 1980s and 90s brought accessible sports watches such as the Formula 1 and a long partnership with McLaren. LVMH bought the company in 1999.

In the 2010s TAG Heuer launched in-house chronograph movements, notably the Heuer 01 and Heuer 02, and in 2015 the Connected smartwatch. Since 2020 it has refocused on its heritage, with the glassbox Carrera and the TH20-00 movement, and returned as official timekeeper of Formula 1 in 2025. It is headquartered in La Chaux-de-Fonds.

name: Breitling
tagline: Instruments for professionals: the aviator's chronograph since 1884
summary: Breitling is an independent Swiss brand best known for pilot chronographs such as the slide-rule Navitimer. Once the chronograph specialist of the aviation world, it has been repositioned since 2017 as a 'modern retro' casual-luxury brand with in-house B01 movements.
history:
Léon Breitling opened a workshop in Saint-Imier in 1884 to make chronographs and timing instruments, moving to Grenchen in 1892. His son Gaston created one of the first wrist chronographs with a separate pusher at 2 o'clock in 1915, and grandson Willy added an independent return-to-zero pusher in 1934, establishing the modern two-pusher layout.

Breitling became a favourite of aviators. The Chronomat of 1942 added a circular slide rule, and the Navitimer of 1952, adopted by the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association, turned it into a flight computer for the wrist. Astronaut Scott Carpenter wore a 24-hour Navitimer Cosmonaute on Mercury-Atlas 7 in 1962. In 1969 Breitling co-developed the automatic Calibre 11 with Heuer, Hamilton-Büren and Dubois Dépraz.

The quartz crisis forced Willy Breitling to close the firm in 1979. Pilot and electronics entrepreneur Ernest Schneider bought the name and relaunched it from Grenchen, bringing a revived Chronomat in 1984 and the Emergency, with a built-in distress beacon, in 1995. By 2002 every Breitling was COSMOC-certified as a chronometer, and in 2009 it introduced its in-house B01 chronograph calibre.

In 2017 the Schneider family sold a majority to private-equity firm CVC Capital Partners and Georges Kern became CEO, reshaping the catalogue around the Navitimer, Chronomat, Superocean and Premier and a retro-casual image. Partners Group took a significant stake in 2021 and majority control in 2022, with CVC retaining a minority. Breitling remains headquartered in Grenchen.

name: IWC Schaffhausen
tagline: Engineering-led pilot's watches and Portugiesers from Switzerland's only Rhine-side maker
summary: IWC is a Richemont-owned manufacture in Schaffhausen, founded by an American, and best known for its Pilot's Watches, the Portugieser and the Ingenieur. It is prized for technical watchmaking, from the Pellaton winding system to perpetual calendars.
history:
The International Watch Company was founded in 1868 by Florentine Ariosto Jones, a watchmaker from Boston who planned to combine cheap Swiss labour with American industrial methods. Unusually, he chose German-speaking Schaffhausen in north-eastern Switzerland, where industrialist Heinrich Moser's Rhine hydropower plant could drive machinery. Jones's venture struggled, and in 1880 the Rauschenbach family took control; the family and their descendants, including Ernst Jakob Homberger, ran IWC for nearly a century.

IWC built a reputation for robust, precise movements. The Pallweber pocket watches of 1884 showed the time with jumping digital numerals. In 1936 it launched its first Special Pilot's Watch, followed in 1939 by the large-cased Portugieser ordered by two Portuguese merchants, and in 1940 by the 55mm Big Pilot's Watch for the German air force. The Mark 11 of 1948 served the Royal Air Force for decades. Technical director Albert Pellaton developed his efficient pawl winding system in 1950, used in the antimagnetic Ingenieur of 1955.

The quartz crisis led to IWC's sale to the German VDO Adolf Schindling group in 1978. Under Günter Blümlein, IWC made titanium watches for Porsche Design and in 1985 launched Kurt Klaus's Da Vinci perpetual calendar, which could be set entirely by the crown. IWC joined Jaeger-LeCoultre and A. Lange & Söhne in LMH, which was acquired by Richemont in 2000.

Under Richemont IWC expanded its in-house calibres, including the 7-day 5000 series and later the 52000 and 82000 families built around Pellaton winding. The Pilot's Watches, Portugieser and a Gérald Genta-inspired Ingenieur revived in 2023 anchor a catalogue that ranges from steel tool watches to grand complications such as the Portugieser Sidérale Scafusia.

name: Panerai
tagline: Florentine naval divers' watches with a cult following
summary: Panerai began as a Florentine supplier of precision instruments to the Italian Navy and now makes its big cushion-cased Luminor and Radiomir watches in Neuchâtel for Richemont. Its crown-protecting bridge and sandwich dials are instantly recognisable.
history:
Giovanni Panerai opened a watch shop and workshop on Florence's Ponte alle Grazie in 1860. His grandson Guido turned the family business towards precision instruments for the Royal Italian Navy, and in 1916 Panerai patented Radiomir, a radium-based luminous paste for gun sights and dials.

In 1936 Panerai built prototype diving watches for the frogmen of the Navy's First Submarine Group Command, using large cushion-shaped cases and movements supplied by Rolex, with Panerai making the luminous dials. The Radiomir went into service in 1938, and wartime experience led to features such as the 'sandwich' dial, with numerals cut through a top plate over a luminous layer. In 1949 Panerai registered Luminor, a tritium-based compound, and in the 1950s patented the lever-operated crown-protecting bridge that defines the Luminor case. The Egiziano, a 60mm giant, was made for the Egyptian Navy in 1956. In total only a few hundred to a few thousand military watches were delivered.

After the military contracts ended, Panerai launched its first civilian collection in 1993. Sylvester Stallone wore a Luminor in the 1996 film Daylight and ordered special editions for friends, spreading the brand in Hollywood. In 1997 the Vendôme group, now Richemont, bought Panerai and turned it into an international luxury brand, relocating production to Switzerland.

Panerai opened a manufacture in Neuchâtel in 2002 and introduced its first in-house calibre, the P.2002, in 2005. Since then it has expanded its in-house movement range and developed materials such as BMG-Tech metallic glass, Carbotech and recycled eSteel. The Luminor, Radiomir, Submersible and Luminor Due collections continue the Italian naval design that attracts devoted collectors known as 'Paneristi'.

name: Zenith
tagline: Home of the El Primero, the high-beat automatic chronograph
summary: Zenith is an LVMH-owned manufacture in Le Locle whose El Primero, unveiled in 1969, was among the first automatic chronograph movements and beats at 36,000 vph. Its Chronomaster and Defy collections carry that high-frequency heritage.
history:
Georges Favre-Jacot founded his watchmaking business in Le Locle in 1865, aged 22, and was among the first to gather the many crafts of watchmaking under one roof in a true manufacture. His pocket-watch calibre named Zenith, launched at the end of the 19th century, was so successful that the company adopted the name in 1911. Zenith became a prolific winner of observatory chronometry prizes and supplied pilots' watches and instruments.

On 10 January 1969 Zenith announced the El Primero, an integrated automatic chronograph movement beating at 36,000 vibrations per hour and able to measure tenths of a second. It was one of the first automatic chronograph calibres, launched in the same year as the Calibre 11 of Heuer and Breitling and Seiko's 6139.

The quartz crisis nearly ended the story. In the 1970s Zenith was owned by the American Zenith Radio Corporation, which ordered mechanical production to be stopped. Workshop head Charles Vermot secretly hid the El Primero tools, plans and cams in an attic, allowing production to restart in the 1980s. From 1988 a modified El Primero powered the Rolex Cosmograph Daytona until 2000.

LVMH bought Zenith in 1999. After a flamboyant period under Thierry Nataf, Jean-Claude Biver and then Julien Tornare refocused the brand on its heritage, and in 2017 Zenith launched the Defy El Primero 21, measuring 1/100th of a second, and the Defy Lab with a silicon monolithic oscillator. Today the Chronomaster Sport, Chronomaster Original, Defy Skyline and Pilot lines are made in the historic Le Locle manufacture.

name: Longines
tagline: Elegance since 1832, under the oldest registered watch logo
summary: Longines is the Swatch Group's classic mid-luxury brand from Saint-Imier, with a long history in aviation, sports timing and elegant dress watches. Its winged hourglass is one of the oldest registered trademarks still in use.
history:
Longines traces its origins to 1832, when Auguste Agassiz joined a watch trading business in Saint-Imier in the Jura. His nephew Ernest Francillon took over and in 1867 brought production under one roof in a factory on a meadow known as 'Les Longines' ('the long fields'). The first movement made there won an award at the Paris Universal Exhibition the same year. The winged hourglass logo was registered in 1889 and is recognised as the oldest unchanged registered trademark for a watch brand.

Longines built its name on precision and sports timing, timing equestrian events and early Olympic Games, and in the 1920s and 30s it became the aviator's brand. It made the Weems Second-Setting Watch for navigator Philip Van Horn Weems and in 1931 the Hour Angle Watch designed with Charles Lindbergh. Amelia Earhart and other pioneer aviators also used Longines. Albert Einstein owned a Longines pocket watch.

The quartz crisis weakened the independent firm, which was sold to General Watch Co. (ASUAG) in 1971. In 1983 ASUAG merged with SSIH to create what became the Swatch Group, and Longines was positioned as its elegant, accessible luxury brand.

Since the 1990s Longines has become one of the Swatch Group's largest brands by volume, with strong sales in China. Its catalogue blends classic lines such as the Master Collection and La Grande Classique with heritage reissues like the Legend Diver and sporty lines such as the Conquest, HydroConquest and the Spirit pilot's watches introduced in 2020. Movements are exclusive ETA-based calibres with silicon balance springs. Longines remains in Saint-Imier, where its museum holds the company's archives.

name: Montblanc
tagline: The pen house whose watches draw on Minerva's Swiss heritage
summary: Montblanc, the German writing-instrument and leather-goods maison owned by Richemont, has made watches since 1997 in Le Locle and, since 2006, at the historic Minerva manufacture in Villeret. Its 1858 line draws on Minerva's mountaineering and military chronographs.
history:
Montblanc was founded in Germany in 1906 as the Simplo Filler Pen Company by stationer Claus-Johannes Voss, banker Alfred Nehemias and engineer August Eberstein. It adopted the Montblanc name, after Europe's highest peak, for its pens around 1910, added the white snowcap emblem in 1913 and in 1924 launched the Meisterstück fountain pen that became its icon. The company is based in Hamburg.

In 1977 Alfred Dunhill Ltd acquired Montblanc, and in 1993 it became part of the Vendôme group, now Richemont. Diversifying beyond pens, Montblanc entered watchmaking in 1997 with Montblanc Montre SA in Le Locle, producing well-finished watches at accessible luxury prices.

The decisive step came in 2006, when Richemont acquired Minerva, a Villeret manufacture founded in 1858 and famed for its chronograph movements. Montblanc created the Institut Minerva de Recherche en Haute Horlogerie there to preserve traditional craft, and in 2008 launched the in-house Nicolas Rieussec monopusher chronograph, named after the inventor credited with an early chronograph. Villeret went on to produce high complications such as the ExoTourbillon and Metamorphosis.

Today Montblanc's watch catalogue centres on the 1858 collection, inspired by Minerva's vintage mountaineering and military watches, including the Geosphere world-timer and the Iced Sea divers with dials textured like glacier ice; the Star Legacy and Heritage dress lines; and the high-end Minerva pieces. Montblanc remains one of the few luxury houses to span pens, leather goods and serious watchmaking.

name: Oris
tagline: Independent Swiss mechanical watches, 'Go your own way' since 1904
summary: Oris is one of the few independent Swiss watch companies, making only mechanical watches, recognisable by the red rotor. Its Aquis and Divers Sixty-Five divers, Big Crown pilot's watches and in-house Calibre 400 offer strong value in the Swiss mid-range.
history:
Oris was founded in 1904 by Paul Cattin and Georges Christian, who bought a disused watch factory in the village of Hölstein near Basel and named their company after a nearby brook. The business grew rapidly, becoming the largest employer in the area and building housing for workers; by the late 1920s it ran several factories. Swiss cartel rules limited Oris to pin-lever escapements until the 1960s, but it still produced hundreds of calibres.

In 1938 Oris launched the Big Crown, a pilot's watch whose oversized crown could be operated with gloves and whose pointer-date hand became a signature. The Divers Sixty-Five of 1965 and early alarm and chronograph models followed. Oris joined the ASUAG conglomerate in 1970, and during the quartz crisis its workforce shrank dramatically.

In 1982 managers Dr Rolf Portmann and Ulrich W. Herzog led a buyout, making Oris independent again. They decided to make only mechanical watches, an unusual bet at the height of the quartz era, adopted the red rotor as a signature and repositioned the brand around four worlds: diving, aviation, motor sport and culture. The Aquis dive watch arrived in 2011 and the Divers Sixty-Five reissue in 2015.

Oris returned to in-house movement making with the hand-wound, ten-day Calibre 110 in 2014 for its 110th anniversary, and in 2020 introduced Calibre 400, an automatic with a five-day power reserve, high anti-magnetism and a ten-year warranty. It has become known for environmental and social projects, such as dials made from upcycled plastic. Oris remains headquartered in Hölstein and privately owned.

name: Rado
tagline: The master of materials, pioneer of scratch-resistant and ceramic watches
summary: Rado is the Swatch Group's materials specialist, famous for scratch-resistant hardmetal and high-tech ceramic watches. Its DiaStar, Captain Cook and True collections combine modern design with durable, lightweight materials.
history:
Rado grew out of Schlup & Co., a movement factory founded in 1917 in Lengnau, near Biel, by brothers Fritz, Ernst and Werner Schlup. For decades it supplied movements to other brands. After the Second World War the company began producing its own watches, and in 1957 it introduced the Rado name with the Golden Horse collection.

Rado found its identity in materials. In 1962 it launched the DiaStar, widely described as the world's first scratch-resistant watch, with a case in hardmetal (a tungsten-carbide alloy) and a faceted sapphire crystal. The same year it introduced the Captain Cook diver. Rado became part of ASUAG in 1971 and, through the 1983 merger with SSIH, part of the Swatch Group.

In 1986 Rado launched the Integral, the first of its watches to use high-tech ceramic for the bracelet, and in 1990 the Ceramica with an all-ceramic case and bracelet. The 1998 V10K used ultra-hard diamond-like coatings, and in 2011 Rado introduced plasma high-tech ceramic, with a metallic grey appearance but no metal content. Other developments included monobloc ceramic cases, the ultra-light Ceramos composite, and colour ceramics.

Rado's recent success has come from the reissued Captain Cook, relaunched in 2017, and the True Square and True Thinline collections, often designed with outside designers such as Tej Chauhan and Konstantin Grcic. Headquartered in Lengnau, Rado remains one of the Swatch Group's key brands in Asia and the Middle East, known for hard-wearing watches at mid-range prices.

name: Tissot
tagline: Swiss watches for everyone, from Le Locle since 1853
summary: Tissot is the Swatch Group's high-volume, accessible Swiss brand, selling millions of watches a year. It is known for innovations such as the first mass-produced dual-time pocket watch and the T-Touch, and for the hugely popular PRX.
history:
Charles-Félicien Tissot and his son Charles-Émile founded Tissot in Le Locle in 1853, assembling watches from parts made by local craftsmen. That same year they produced what the company describes as the first mass-produced pocket watch showing two time zones. Charles-Émile travelled to Russia and the Americas to sell the watches, and Russia became a major market; Tissot supplied watches to the Russian Imperial court.

In 1930 Tissot introduced one of the first antimagnetic wristwatches and in the same year merged with Omega to form SSIH, the Société Suisse pour l'Industrie Horlogère. Tissot became SSIH's more affordable brand. It experimented widely: the Navigator world-time watch of 1953, the Sideral of 1971 with a fibreglass case, and the Astrolon or IDEA 2001 of 1971, the first mechanical watch with a movement made largely of plastic. The quartz crisis led to the 1983 merger of SSIH and ASUAG that created the Swatch Group.

In the 1980s Tissot released unconventional materials watches such as the RockWatch in Alpine granite, WoodWatch and PearlWatch. In 1999 came the T-Touch, a tactile-screen analogue watch with altimeter, compass and barometer, which evolved into the solar T-Touch Connect.

Tissot's volume rests on sponsorships including MotoGP, cycling and basketball and on the Powermatic 80 movement, introduced in 2013, which gave an 80-hour power reserve at mass-market prices. The 2021 PRX, based on a 1978 integrated-bracelet design, became a global hit and one of the best-selling Swiss watches of the decade. Tissot remains headquartered in Le Locle.

name: Baume & Mercier
tagline: Accessible Geneva elegance with roots stretching back to 1830
summary: Baume & Mercier is a Geneva watchmaker known for classic, accessible luxury watches such as the Riviera, Clifton and Hampton. Owned by Richemont from 1988, it was sold to Italy's Damiani Group in 2026.
history:
The Baume family set up a watchmaking business in Les Bioux, in the Swiss Jura, in 1830, and brothers Louis-Victor and Célestin Baume founded Frères Baume, later opening a London branch, Baume Brothers, in 1844. The firm built a reputation for precise pocket watches and complications, winning prizes at observatory trials and international exhibitions in the late 19th century.

In 1918 William Baume went into partnership with Paul Mercier, a watch dealer of Russian origin, and the Maison Baume & Mercier was registered in Geneva in 1919, earning the Geneva Hallmark for its watches. The company focused on elegant wristwatches and, in the 1920s and 30s, on watches for women. In 1964 it adopted the Greek letter phi, symbol of the golden ratio, as its emblem, and in 1965 Piaget took control.

The quartz era brought the 1973 Riviera, an integrated-bracelet sports watch with a twelve-sided bezel, followed by the rectangular Hampton in 1994 and the Classima, Capeland and Clifton lines. In 1988 the Vendôme group, later Richemont, acquired Baume & Mercier, positioning it as the group's entry point to Swiss luxury.

In 2018 the brand introduced the Baumatic, an automatic movement with a five-day power reserve and silicon components developed with Richemont's ValFleurier manufacture. Sales, however, lagged behind rivals. In January 2026 Richemont agreed to sell the brand to the Italian jeweller Damiani Group, and the transaction closed on 1 July 2026, with Richemont providing operational services for a transitional period. The Riviera, relaunched in 2021, remains its best-known design.

name: Raymond Weil
tagline: Family-owned Geneva watchmaker inspired by music and the arts
summary: Raymond Weil is an independent, family-run Geneva brand founded in 1976, known for accessible Swiss watches whose collections are named after music and opera. It is now led by the founder's grandson, Elie Bernheim.
history:
Raymond Weil founded his company in Geneva in 1976, in the middle of the quartz crisis, after more than two decades in the watch industry, together with partner Simone Bédat. Betting that there was room for an independent brand, he offered well-made Swiss watches, initially mostly quartz, at accessible prices, and built a distribution network across dozens of countries.

Weil's love of the arts shaped the brand's identity. Early collections included Golden Eagle and Amadeus, and later lines were given musical and operatic names such as Othello, Fidelio, Parsifal, Tango, Toccata and Maestro. The ultra-thin Othello of 1983 and the gold-and-steel Parsifal of 1988 were among its early successes, and the brand became well known for advertising and for partnerships with musicians and music institutions.

The company remained in family hands. Weil's son-in-law Olivier Bernheim became president in 1996, and in 2014, the year Raymond Weil died, his grandson Elie Bernheim became CEO, with his brother Pierre Bernheim also in the business. Under the third generation the brand developed limited editions with music icons such as the Beatles, David Bowie, AC/DC and Gibson guitars.

In 2016 Raymond Weil introduced Calibre RW1212, its first in-house-developed movement made in collaboration with Sellita, featuring an open balance, in the Freelancer sports collection. Recent years have brought the Millesime vintage-inspired line and new integrated-bracelet Freelancers. Raymond Weil remains independent and headquartered in Geneva, one of the few family-owned Swiss brands of its size.

name: Frederique Constant
tagline: Accessible Geneva manufacture watches, from Heart Beat to perpetual calendars
summary: Frederique Constant is a Geneva brand founded in 1988 by a Dutch couple with the aim of making 'accessible luxury'. It is known for in-house movements at unusually low prices, including moonphases and perpetual calendars, and has been owned by Citizen since 2016.
history:
Frederique Constant was founded in Geneva in 1988 by Peter Stas and Aletta Bax, a Dutch couple who wanted to offer traditionally crafted Swiss watches at accessible prices. They named the brand after two ancestors: Frédérique Schreiner, Aletta's great-grandmother, and Ferdinand Constant Stas, Peter's great-grandfather, who had run a clock-dial business. The first watches were assembled in small numbers and sold mainly in Europe and Asia.

The brand's breakthrough came in 1994 with the Heart Beat, whose dial aperture revealed the beating balance wheel, a feature that became a signature. Frederique Constant then set out to make its own movements, presenting the in-house Heart Beat Manufacture calibre FC-910 in 2004 and gradually developing a family of manufacture calibres, including chronographs, moonphases, a worldtimer and a tourbillon. In 2002 the company also bought the historic sports-watch brand Alpina, and it later moved into a larger manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates, Geneva.

Frederique Constant earned a reputation for value: its Slimline Perpetual Calendar Manufacture, launched in 2016, was one of the most affordable Swiss in-house perpetual calendars. It also experimented with technology, launching a Horological Smartwatch in 2015 that kept an analogue display while tracking activity and sleep.

In 2016 the Stas family sold Frederique Constant, together with Alpina and Ateliers deMonaco, to Japan's Citizen Watch Co., with Peter Stas staying on for a period. In 2021 the brand unveiled the Slimline Monolithic Manufacture with a high-frequency flexure-based silicon oscillator. The Classics, Slimline, Highlife and Manufacture lines remain its core.

name: Maurice Lacroix
tagline: Swiss watches from the Jura, home of the Aikon
summary: Maurice Lacroix is a Swiss brand created in 1975 by the trading company Desco von Schulthess and majority-owned by DKSH since 2011. Its integrated-bracelet Aikon is one of the best-selling watches in its price range, alongside the complicated Masterpiece line.
history:
Maurice Lacroix was launched in 1975 by Desco von Schulthess, a Zurich-based trading company that had been distributing watches and components and decided to create its own brand. The name was borrowed from a respected former company executive. Production was based in the Jura village of Saignelégier, where the company had taken over a watch assembly workshop, and the first watches were quartz and simple mechanical designs sold mainly in Europe.

The brand grew steadily through the 1980s and 1990s with accessible dress and sports watches. In 1990 it introduced the Calypso, a sports watch with an integrated bracelet and a bezel with six 'claws', which would later inspire the Aikon. The Masterpiece line, launched in the early 1990s, became the platform for more ambitious mechanical watches and complications.

In 2006 Maurice Lacroix presented its first in-house movement, the ML106 chronograph calibre, and began building a manufacture in the Jura, later adding eye-catching complications such as the Roue Carrée with square and cloverleaf-shaped wheels and a mysterious seconds display. In 2011 the Swiss market-expansion group DKSH, which had grown out of Desco von Schulthess, acquired a majority stake. DKSH has repeatedly explored a sale of the brand.

The Aikon, launched in 2016, transformed the company's fortunes. Its integrated bracelet and claw bezel offered a sport-luxury look at a fraction of the price of more famous designs, and the line expanded to automatics, chronographs, skeletons, ultra-thin models and the Aikon #tide made from recycled ocean plastic. Today the company is headquartered in Zurich with production in the Jura.

name: Carl F. Bucherer
tagline: Lucerne's watchmaker of the peripheral rotor, now under Rolex ownership
summary: Carl F. Bucherer is the watch brand of the Lucerne jeweller Bucherer, known for its peripheral-rotor Manero and Patravi watches. Rolex acquired it with the Bucherer retail group in 2023, and in 2025 reports said the brand would be phased out.
history:
Carl Friedrich Bucherer and his wife opened a watch and jewellery shop in Lucerne in 1888, laying the foundation of what became Bucherer, one of Europe's largest watch retailers. The family began selling watches under its own name in 1919 with a collection of Art Deco ladies' watches, and later produced chronographs and certified chronometers; by the 1950s and 60s it was a notable producer of COSC-certified watches, and in 1969 it joined the consortium that developed the Beta 21 quartz movement.

For decades the watches were sold chiefly through the family's own stores. In 2001, under third-generation owner Jörg G. Bucherer, the brand was relaunched internationally as Carl F. Bucherer, with the sporty Patravi collection. In 2007 it acquired movement maker Techniques Horlogères Appliquées (THA) in Sainte-Croix, and in 2008 it unveiled the CFB A1000, a manufacture calibre with a peripheral rotor running around the edge of the movement, allowing an unobstructed view and a slimmer construction. The Manero, Patravi, Heritage and Adamavi collections followed, with prices broadly between about CHF 5,000 and 30,000.

The brand, estimated to make tens of thousands of watches a year, never achieved profitability, surviving largely as Jörg Bucherer's passion. In August 2023 Rolex announced it would buy the Bucherer group, including the watch brand; Jörg Bucherer died shortly afterwards. In February 2025 Swiss media reported that Rolex had decided to shut Carl F. Bucherer down, with its roughly 250 points of sale to be phased out and staff offered roles within Rolex. Bucherer called the reports rumours, and the brand's website remained online into 2026, so its long-term status is uncertain.

name: Ebel
tagline: The 'architects of time' and their wave-link bracelets
summary: Ebel is a La Chaux-de-Fonds watchmaker founded in 1911 and owned by the Movado Group since 2004. It is best known for the 1977 Sport Classic with its wave-shaped bracelet links and five-screw bezel, and for the Beluga ladies' watches.
history:
Ebel was founded in 1911 in La Chaux-de-Fonds by husband and wife Eugène Blum and Alice Lévy, and its name is formed from their initials: Eugène Blum et Lévy. Alice Lévy was closely involved in design and the business, and the company quickly established itself as a maker of fine watches. Their son Charles Blum took over in 1929 and expanded international sales.

The third generation, Pierre-Alain Blum, took charge in 1970 and transformed the company. Ebel manufactured watches for Cartier and, in 1977, launched the Sport Classic, whose integrated bracelet of wave-shaped links and screwed bezel became the brand's signature. In the early 1980s Ebel bought a stock of El Primero chronograph components from Zenith, producing its Calibre 134 chronograph, and Pierre-Alain Blum marketed the brand with the slogan 'the architects of time'. For the company's 75th anniversary in 1986, Ebel bought and restored the Villa Turque, designed by Le Corbusier in La Chaux-de-Fonds. Don Johnson's Sonny Crockett wore an Ebel on Miami Vice, and the 1911 chronograph and Beluga became hits of the 1980s and 90s.

The boom did not last. Ebel was sold to the investment firm Investcorp in 1994 and to LVMH in 1999. In 2004 the Movado Group bought it, repositioning Ebel as an accessible luxury brand with a strong focus on women's watches.

Today Ebel's collections centre on the Sport Classic, the Wave and the Beluga, with most models quartz-powered and sold through the Movado Group's distribution network.

name: Eterna
tagline: The Grenchen innovator that gave birth to ETA
summary: Eterna is a Grenchen watchmaker founded in 1856 whose movement division became ETA, today the backbone of the Swatch Group. Famous for the ball-bearing Eterna-Matic rotor and the KonTiki divers, it has been owned by Hong Kong's Citychamp group since 2011.
history:
Eterna was founded on 7 November 1856 in Grenchen by physician Dr Josef Girard and teacher Urs Schild as the ébauche workshop Dr. Girard & Schild. The company became Schild Frères & Co. and, after launching its own finished watches, adopted the Eterna name in 1905. It was an early innovator: in 1908 it patented one of the first wristwatch alarms, and it made some of the earliest wristwatches for women.

In 1932, amid restructuring of the Swiss watch industry, Eterna's movement production was separated into a distinct company, ETA. ETA went on to become the dominant supplier of Swiss movements and, through ASUAG and the 1983 merger with SSIH, the industrial core of the Swatch Group, while Eterna continued as a watch brand.

In 1948 Eterna introduced the Eterna-Matic, whose rotor ran on five tiny ball bearings to reduce friction; the five balls became the brand's logo. When Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft expedition crossed the Pacific, Eterna watches were aboard, and in 1958 the brand launched the KonTiki sports watch, followed by divers such as the Super KonTiki. The Eterna-Matic 3000 Dato of 1962 was billed as the thinnest automatic men's watch with a date.

After the quartz crisis Eterna changed hands several times. In 1995 it was bought by the Porsche family, and it manufactured Porsche Design watches until the partnership ended in 2014. In 2011 it was acquired by China Haidian, later renamed Citychamp Watch & Jewellery Group. Eterna remains based in Grenchen, focusing on KonTiki, Heritage and Eternity collections; unlike stablemate Corum, it stayed with Citychamp after 2025.

name: Mido
tagline: 'I measure': Swiss chronometers inspired by architecture
summary: Mido is a Swatch Group brand founded in Biel in 1918, known for robust automatic watches, many COSC-certified, inspired by architecture. Its Ocean Star divers, Multifort and Commander lines offer strong value.
history:
Georges G. Schaeren founded Mido in Biel/Bienne in 1918, choosing a name from the Spanish 'Yo mido', meaning 'I measure'. In the 1920s Mido became known for colourful, shaped Art Deco watches and for novelty designs such as watches shaped like car radiator grilles for brands including Bugatti and Buick.

The company focused on durability. In 1934 it launched the Multifort, a self-winding watch that was also antimagnetic, shock-resistant and water-resistant, qualities then rarely combined. Mido also developed the Aquadura crown-sealing system, which uses natural cork to seal the winding stem against water. The Ocean Star arrived in 1944 as a water-resistant sports watch and later became Mido's diving line, and in 1959 Mido launched the Commander, with a monobloc case, which was produced continuously for decades.

Like many Swiss firms, Mido was hit by the quartz crisis. It joined ASUAG's General Watch Co. in 1971 and became part of the Swatch Group through the 1983 merger of ASUAG and SSIH. Within the group it was positioned as a mechanical-watch specialist at accessible prices, with a particular following in Latin America and Asia.

Since the 2000s Mido has built its identity around architecture, drawing inspiration from landmarks such as the Golden Gate Bridge, the Colosseum and the Sydney Opera House for its Multifort, Baroncelli, Commander and Ocean Star designs. It became one of the largest producers of COSC-certified chronometers and uses Swatch Group movements such as the Caliber 80 with an 80-hour power reserve and silicon balance spring. Mido is headquartered in Le Locle.

name: Certina
tagline: Double Security: Swatch Group sports watches built to last
summary: Certina is a Swatch Group brand founded in Grenchen in 1888 and known for its DS (Double Security) concept of shock- and water-resistant watches. Its DS Action and DS PH divers and turtle logo target sporty, value-minded buyers.
history:
Brothers Adolf and Alfred Kurth founded Kurth Frères in Grenchen in 1888, making watch movements in a small workshop. The company prospered and in 1906 began selling finished watches under the name Grana. In 1938 it introduced the name Certina, from the Latin 'certus', meaning certain or assured, and after the Second World War Certina became the main brand.

By the 1950s Certina employed several hundred people and produced around a thousand watches a day. Its defining innovation arrived in 1959 with the DS, for Double Security: a construction that combined a shock-absorbing suspended movement with reinforced case, crystal and gaskets, making the watches unusually resistant to impacts and water. The turtle emblem, symbol of longevity and protection, became the DS signature. The DS-2 and DS PH200M diver followed in the late 1960s, and in 1971 Certina launched the Biostar, a watch that displayed the wearer's biorhythms.

The quartz crisis pushed Certina into the General Watch Co. of ASUAG in 1971, and through the 1983 merger with SSIH it became part of what is now the Swatch Group. Within the group Certina focuses on sporty, robust watches at accessible prices, often with Powermatic 80 movements and silicon balance springs.

Certina has built a following through heritage reissues such as the DS PH200M and DS Super PH500M, and through the DS Action range of divers and chronographs. It has long been associated with motor sport and diving, and the brand is now based in Le Locle.

name: Hamilton
tagline: American spirit, Swiss precision: the field watch and film-star brand
summary: Hamilton was founded in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and made railroad and military watches before moving to Switzerland and joining the Swatch Group. Its Khaki Field watches, the triangular Ventura and frequent film appearances make it a favourite affordable brand.
history:
The Hamilton Watch Company was founded in 1892 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, taking over the premises of earlier watch firms and taking its name from Andrew Hamilton, who had once owned the land. It became known for highly accurate pocket watches for the American railroads, where precise timekeeping was a matter of safety, and at its peak supplied a large share of railroad-grade watches.

Hamilton became the official watch supplier to the US armed forces. In the First World War it made wristwatches for American soldiers, and in the Second World War it halted civilian production to make watches and precision marine chronometers for the military. Those rugged, legible designs inspired today's Khaki Field line. In 1918 Hamilton watches were used on the first US airmail flights.

In 1957 Hamilton launched the Ventura, the world's first battery-powered electric wristwatch, in a triangular case designed by Richard Arbib; Elvis Presley wore one in the 1961 film Blue Hawaii. In 1966 Hamilton bought the Swiss firm Büren, which had pioneered the micro-rotor, and in 1969 it helped introduce the Calibre 11 automatic chronograph. In 1970 it unveiled the Pulsar, the first LED digital watch. American production wound down, and in 1974 the brand was sold to the Swiss SSIH group, which in 1983 merged into what became the Swatch Group.

Now headquartered in Biel/Bienne, Hamilton uses Swatch Group movements such as the H-10 with 80-hour power reserve. It has appeared in more than 500 films, including 2001: A Space Odyssey, Men in Black and Interstellar, whose Murph watch became a production model. The Khaki Field Mechanical, Khaki Navy Scuba, Jazzmaster and American Classic PSR are among its best-known models.

name: Movado
tagline: 'Always in motion': home of the minimalist Museum dial
summary: Movado is a Swiss-founded brand now owned by the US-based Movado Group, famous for the minimalist Museum dial with a single dot at 12 o'clock. It sells mainly quartz fashion-luxury watches such as the Museum Classic and Bold.
history:
Movado's roots go back to 1881, when 19-year-old Achille Ditesheim opened a watchmaking workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds. His brothers Léopold and Isidore joined him, and in 1892 the firm became L.A. & I. Ditesheim, one of the area's first modern watch factories. Around 1905 it adopted the name Movado, Esperanto for 'always in motion'.

Movado was an innovative Swiss maker in the first half of the 20th century. In 1912 it introduced the Polyplan, a curved rectangular watch whose movement was built on three levels to fit the curve of the wrist, and in the 1920s and 30s it made the Ermeto, a purse watch wound by opening and closing its sliding case. Movado chronographs and calendar watches were widely admired.

In 1947 American designer Nathan George Horwitt created a dial with no numerals, only a single dot at 12 o'clock representing the sun at noon. Movado adopted it, and in 1960 the Museum of Modern Art in New York added Horwitt's design to its permanent collection, giving the Museum Watch its name. In 1969 Movado joined Zenith and Mondia in a holding company, and the Datron automatic chronograph used the El Primero movement.

In 1983 the North American Watch Corporation, founded by Cuban-born entrepreneur Gedalio Grinberg, bought Movado; the parent company later took the name Movado Group and is headquartered in Paramus, New Jersey, led by the founder's son Efraim Grinberg. Movado Group also owns Ebel, Olivia Burton and MVMT and holds licences for fashion brands. Today the Movado brand focuses on quartz Museum Classic and Bold watches sold in department stores and its own outlets.

name: Alpina
tagline: Swiss sports watches born in the Alps, from pilot's watches to divers
summary: Alpina is a sports-watch brand with roots in the 1883 Swiss Watchmakers Corporation, known for the 1938 Alpina 4 and for pilot's and dive watches. Revived by Frederique Constant in 2002, it has been owned by Citizen since 2016.
history:
Alpina traces its origins to 1883, when watchmaker Gottlieb Hauser founded the Swiss Watchmakers Corporation, a cooperative of independent watchmakers and suppliers. The group grew into Alpina Union Horlogère, one of the larger Swiss watch associations of the early 20th century, with a presence in Switzerland and Germany, where its German branch had factories in Glashütte.

In 1938 Alpina introduced the Alpina 4, a sports watch built around four principles: an antimagnetic movement, shock resistance, water resistance and a stainless-steel case. It became the basis for Alpina's later sports and dive watches, including the Seastrong divers. Alpina also made pilot's watches, and its German branch produced aviation watches in the 1930s. After the Second World War the German operation was separated and later became the Dugena brand, and as the quartz crisis deepened Alpina largely disappeared from view.

The brand was revived in 2002 when Peter and Aletta Stas, founders of Frederique Constant, acquired it. They repositioned Alpina as a Swiss sports-watch brand focused on mountaineering, aviation and diving, with collections such as the Alpiner, Startimer and Seastrong, and introduced in-house calibres developed alongside Frederique Constant's manufacture in Plan-les-Ouates. In 2016 both brands were sold to Japan's Citizen.

Alpina drew attention with the AlpinerX outdoor smartwatch in 2018 and, in 2020, with the Alpiner Extreme, an integrated-bracelet sports watch inspired by its 1970s designs. Recent models include solar Solarmetre versions and the 39mm Seastrong Diver Extreme. Alpina's watches carry a red triangle logo that represents the Alps.
